static_findings.snippet: This skill describes how to write docstrings for functions and methods in the PyTorch project, follo
- Use **raw strings** (`r"""..."""`) for all docstrings to avoid issues with LaTeX/math backslashes
- Show positional and keyword-only arguments (use `*` separator)
- The `~` prefix shows only the last component (e.g., `Conv2d` instead of `torch.nn.Conv2d`)
See :class:`~torch.nn.Conv2d` for details and output shape.
:func:`new_tensor` always copies :attr:`data`. If you have a Tensor
``data`` and want to avoid a copy, use :func:`torch.Tensor.requires_grad_`

weight (Tensor): filters of shape :math:`(\text{out\_channels} , kH , kW)`
bias (Tensor, optional): optional bias tensor of shape :math:`(\text{out\_channels})`. Default: ``No
- Type in parentheses: `(Type)`, `(Type, optional)` for optional parameters
- For optional parameters, include "Default: ``value``" at the end
- Use double backticks for inline code: ``` ``None`` ```
dtype (:class:`torch.dtype`, optional): the desired type of returned tensor.
Default: if None, same :class:`torch.dtype` as this tensor.
device (:class:`torch.device`, optional): the desired device of returned tensor.
Default: if None, same :class:`torch.device` as this tensor.

content.user_title: Write PyTorch Docstrings in Project Style
content.value_statement: PyTorch contributors need docstrings that match project formatting and Sphinx conventions. This skill guides signatures, arguments, examples, math notation, and references for consistent PyTorch API documentation.
actual_capabilities: Shows PyTorch docstring structure for signatures, descriptions, arguments, returns, notes, warnings, and examples.
Explains raw string usage for docstrings that contain LaTeX, math notation, or Sphinx roles.
Provides Sphinx role patterns for classes, functions, methods, attributes, math, and references.
Describes conventions for C-bound functions, in-place variants, aliases, and reusable argument definitions.
Supplies a checklist for reviewing PyTorch docstrings before submission.
limitations: Does not inspect a repository or modify files by itself.
Does not validate documentation builds or run Sphinx checks.
Does not guarantee that examples execute against every PyTorch version.
Focuses on PyTorch conventions, not general Python docstring styles.

use_cases.title: Document a New Operator
use_cases.description: A PyTorch contributor drafts a docstring with the correct signature, argument list, examples, and related references.

use_cases.title: Review API Documentation
use_cases.description: A maintainer checks whether an updated docstring follows PyTorch formatting, math, and Sphinx conventions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Generated Docs
use_cases.description: A documentation engineer aligns multiple API entries with shared argument definitions, examples, notes, and warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Docstring
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a PyTorch-style docstring for this function. Include a signature line, short description, Args section, and one example.

prompt_templates.title: Add Sphinx References
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this PyTorch docstring with Sphinx class, function, method, and math references where they help readers.

prompt_templates.title: Review for PyTorch Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PyTorch docstring against project conventions. List missing sections, formatting issues, unclear parameters, and example improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Shared Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor these related PyTorch docstrings to reuse common argument text, preserve behavior, and keep examples consistent.

output_examples.input: A request to document a new convolution helper.
output_examples.output: A PyTorch-style docstring outline with a signature, concise description, argument descriptions, return details, and an example plan.

output_examples.input: A docstring with missing cross-references and unclear optional arguments.
output_examples.output: A review summary naming the missing Sphinx links, default value issues, and clearer wording for optional parameters.

output_examples.input: Several related tensor factory functions with repeated parameter text.
output_examples.output: A documentation plan that consolidates shared dtype and device descriptions while preserving function-specific examples.

best_practices: Include a complete signature line before the descriptive text.
Use raw strings when docstrings contain math, escapes, or Sphinx roles.
Add focused examples that show normal use and important options.
anti_patterns: Do not omit default values for optional parameters.
Do not mix NumPy, Google, and PyTorch docstring styles in one entry.
Do not add external links unless they improve reader understanding.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It guides docstring content and examples for PyTorch APIs.

faq.question: Can it update existing PyTorch docstrings?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help revise wording, structure, examples, and cross-references.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No. The guide includes conventions and example reference patterns.

faq.question: Can it validate Sphinx builds?
faq.answer: No. Run the project documentation checks separately.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful outside PyTorch?
faq.answer: Only partly. The guidance is tailored to PyTorch documentation conventions.
